sections.title: Sound of Jot
paragraphs: You call this letter (Jot) /jɔt/. Its main sound is in (Jahr) /jaːɐ̯/, which means year. This letter has three different sounds.

sections.title: Pronouncing Jot
paragraphs: Raise the middle of your tongue close to the hard roof of your mouth. Let the voiced air flow smoothly through the gap. For the second sound, push your lips forward and blow voiced air over the tongue ridge. For the third sound, stop the air first behind the teeth, then release it with voice into that hiss. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the voice buzz.

sections.title: Spelling of Jot
paragraphs: In native German words, you say the first sound, as in (jung) /jʊŋ/. In loanwords from French, you say the smooth hiss, as in (Journalist) /ʒʊʁnaˈlɪst/, or in (Jalousie) /ʒaluˈziː/. In loanwords from English, you say the sound that begins with a stop, as in (Job) /dʒɔp/, or in (Jeans) /dʒiːns/.

sections.title: Comparing Jot
paragraphs: Do not read native German words with the English sound from jam. That sound belongs only to foreign words like (Job) /dʒɔp/. For standard words, use the starting sound from yes. Keep the air flowing smoothly without any hard push or stop.
